title: WP58 completeness table omits the entry-final-scan timing of owner-selected exits
finding: WP58 §5.2 declares a complete source map, but places EJECTPACK and EMERGENCYEXIT/WIMPOUT only in the attack-stage row and couples that row to an already-recorded original action/no further action. Current accepted WP41 §4.2, WP49 §3/§5.1 and WP50 §2/§5.2 include entry-final-scan consumers and distinguish end-of-round deferral from owner choice at other times. In particular opening entry can choose before the first command. The generic every-return append sentence is correct; the phase/source table does not accurately describe this known consumer. Naming the item/ability in an attack row does not resolve its entry timing.
consequence: A replacement implementation following the purported complete table may record or consume at the wrong phase, or omit an opening choice. This is a static specification completeness defect and conditional implementation risk, not an observed playback failure.

unexecuted_static_counterexample.mode: Symbolic static interface prestate; no Ruby, game, reference code or vector executed.
preconditions: Legal ordinary Tower trainer single battle; internalBattle=false; opening normal all-entry procedure before the first command, recorded initial attributes already taken.
Alive active EJECTPACK holder, item effective; entry effects cause a genuine stat-drop event (e.g. a qualifying opposing Intimidate). Do not infer this merely from the presence of an ability name.

Opponent party not all fainted; holder not SkyDrop-held/using SkyDrop; ordinary leave gate true; healthy non-egg same-owner off-field reserve at party index1; no earlier exit ends the first-true scan.
Reserve and entry chain selected so no additional exiting event/terminal decision intervenes; owner returns1.
unexecuted_static_counterexample.static_expected_transition: Entry final scan consumes EJECTPACK before owner selection; choice1 is appended before any first command slot. Playback reaches that same entry consumer and takes1 from the switch sequence, not the random sequence. Clearing an old choice at startup does not itself mean the replacement cannot choose in the upcoming first command.
nearby_negative_controls: No real stat drop, inactive item or no legal reserve: do not invent the corresponding choice.
End-of-round EJECTPACK/exit ability: recall/leave now, reserve selection at later replacement consumer, not an immediate attack-stage choice.
BatonPass W24 attack choice, random Roar/RedCard distinction, Arena candidate=false and W16 internalBattle gate retain their existing meanings.
unexecuted_static_counterexample.ability_neighbor: Entry-hazard crossing of strict integer half plus an effective EmergencyExit/WimpOut, with its existing trainer/candidate/leave gates, is the corresponding entry-timing branch; it must not be generalized to every HP loss.

Add one unexecuted entry-timing acceptance design and a static transition trace/consumer navigation; update only dependent count/identity metadata and the affected-input list to include current WP41, WP49 and WP50 main contracts.
